RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The gender composition of the panel alone is not evidence of bias. Academic hiring committees rarely decide positions based solely on publication count or PhD completion. They weigh interview performance, departmental fit, teaching evaluations, and specific expertise—such as the industry experience highlighted in the announcement. Public institutions also operate under structured HR rubrics to prevent bias.

Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of procedural irregularities or discrimination will be seen as unsubstantiated and could severely damage your professional reputation and future job prospects. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up request for constructive feedback focused entirely on how you can strengthen your application for future openings.
